sophie: Escalation from customer 9987 — JS SDK v2.4.1, mobile webview (iOS 16.8). They start a streaming SSE chat to /v1/streams/chat and the stream consistently stops after ~12-20s when the phone locks or flips between Wi‑Fi/4G. Client sees EOF and partial JSON payloads. Attaching their short repro and logs below.

maya: Thanks — can you paste the minimal repro + the client console and server logs? Which SDK and endpoint exactly?

sophie: Endpoint: POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/chat?model=redwood-1 (SSE). SDK: our JS web client v2.4.1 used inside a webview. Customer console: "net::ERR_CONNECTION_ABORTED". Server-side (nginx/runtime) log excerpt: "stream 9987: client closed after 17s, remote_addr=10.2.3.45 read: connection reset by peer". Customer provided this minimal repro curl they ran from laptop (to simulate):

```bash
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \  -H "Cache-Control: no-cache" \  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/chat?model=redwood-1 \  -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hello"}]}'
```

(When they background the webview on the phone or lock the device, the stream dies around 15s.)

alex: Quick hypothesis: this looks like the mobile OS aggressively tearing down idle TCP sockets when the app is backgrounded or switching networks. iOS is known to send a TCP RST on certain background transitions for webviews. If the client or intermediary doesn't send periodic data, the kernel may drop the connection.

maya: Any server-side mitigations we can try short-term? Customer needs a fix today if possible.

alex: Two pragmatic options:
- Server-side heartbeat: emit SSE "comment" pings (lines starting with ":") every ~10s to keep the TCP flow alive. Low risk, small bytes.
- Client-side keepalive: have the client send tiny activity (a comment or noop fetch) periodically while the page is backgrounded. Not always possible in webviews.

Example server-side ping (SSE):

```: keepalive

```

This is what many SSE servers use to prevent NAT/OS from idling the socket.

sophie: Can we enable a per-customer canary flag to turn on SSE pings for only 9987? What's the rollout and rollback cost?

alex: Low. We can add a feature-flag controlled ping loop in the SSE handler in eng-runtime. Implementation: send ":\n\n" every 10s with the normal chunking logic. Need to watch buffering in proxies; ensure nginx doesn't buffer the connection.

maya: I'll coordinate. Also suggested quick workaround for the customer: switch to the WebSocket shim in our SDK (if they can) — websockets survive some transitions better than long SSE streams in certain webviews.

sophie: Repro steps for eng to validate on device:
1) Open page in iOS webview (16.8) running SDK v2.4.1.
2) Start SSE stream.
3) Lock screen or toggle Wi‑Fi off then on within 20s.
4) Observe stream close / net::ERR_CONNECTION_ABORTED.

Tools/commands we asked them to capture:
- Browser console logs (network tab)
- Full nginx/runtime request id (they gave request id: r-9987-202603)
- tcpdump on proxy if we need packet-level confirmation

support-bot: Ticket created: SUP-3129 (logs attached).

alex: If pinging doesn't clear it, we should capture whether the socket ends with FIN (graceful close) or RST (abort). RST indicates OS-level kill; FIN may indicate app-level close. If we see RST, pings may or may not help. Next debug step: enable tcpdump for a short window and gather a pcapture.

maya: I'm getting customer consent to test the canary flag. I'll also ask them to try a quick client patch: add header 'Connection: keep-alive' and set fetch timeout to infinite (JS side) to rule out SDK abort timers.

sophie: Customer agreed to canary. I've scheduled a small rollout to only their org and will report back in this thread. If we see improvement, we'll propose global opt-in for SSE pings with a runtime config. :thumbsup:

alex: Thanks. If you hit any proxy buffering, pinging won't work — we need to ensure proxies (nginx, CDN) are configured with proxy_buffering off for SSE paths. Add that to the checklist for eng-runtime.

sophie: Noted. I'll add proxy buffer check to SUP-3129.

maya: Great. Thanks all — I'll drive customer comms and follow up with the canary outcome.

sophie: Closing loop later with results. :white_check_mark:
